name: Lockheed Martin C-130J-30 Super Hercules

what_it_is.prose: The Lockheed Martin C-130J-30 Super Hercules is a stretched four-engine turboprop tactical airlifter operated by the Indian Air Force primarily in the special-operations and tactical-transport role. India acquired its first six aircraft via a US Foreign Military Sale in 2008 and ordered a further six in 2013; one aircraft was lost in a 2014 crash near Gwalior, leaving an operational fleet of 12. Lockheed Martin describes the IAF fleet as one of the most active C-130J fleets in the world. India's industrial footprint on the platform is significant: Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures Limited (TLMAL), a Tata Advanced Systems–Lockheed Martin joint venture in Hyderabad, is the single global source of C-130J empennage (tail) assemblies fitted to every new Super Hercules built at Marietta, Georgia; TLMAL has delivered more than 250 empennages since operations began in 2010. Sustainment is covered by a $328.8 million, five-year Follow-On Support II (FOS II) contract signed on 24 August 2021, covering airframe support, spares, engines, propellers and depot maintenance. In 2024 Lockheed Martin and Tata Advanced Systems signed a teaming agreement to establish a C-130J MRO facility in India and, subject to US and Indian government approvals, to expand C-130J manufacturing/assembly in India should the C-130J-30 win the IAF's Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme (60–80 aircraft in the 18–30 tonne class). The aircraft itself remains a US-origin platform powered by Rolls-Royce AE 2100D3 engines; India's role is aerostructure manufacture and sustainment rather than design ownership.

deployments_procurement.summary: India bought six C-130J-30 via a 2008 US FMS and six more in 2013; one was lost in 2014, leaving 12 in service. A $328.8M FOS II sustainment contract was signed in 2021. In 2024 Lockheed Martin and Tata teamed to add C-130J MRO and potential assembly in India, positioning the C-130J-30 for the IAF's MTA competition.

faq.question: How many C-130J does the Indian Air Force operate?
faq.answer: The IAF operates 12 C-130J-30 Super Hercules. India ordered six under a 2008 US Foreign Military Sale and six more in 2013; one aircraft was lost in a 2014 crash, leaving a fleet of 12 — described by Lockheed Martin as one of the most active C-130J fleets in the world.

faq.question: What is India's industrial role in the C-130J?
faq.answer: Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures Limited (TLMAL), a Tata–Lockheed Martin joint venture in Hyderabad, is the single global source of C-130J empennage assemblies fitted to every new Super Hercules. TLMAL has delivered more than 250 empennages since 2010. Lockheed Martin and Tata also signed a 2024 teaming agreement to establish a C-130J MRO facility in India.

faq.question: Is the C-130J a contender in India's next transport tender?
faq.answer: Yes. The C-130J-30, offered with Tata Advanced Systems, is a contender in the IAF's Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme for 60–80 aircraft in the 18–30 tonne class, competing against the Embraer C-390 and (reportedly fading) Airbus A400M. A win could bring C-130J final assembly to India, subject to US and Indian government approvals.
